claim.value: Variable return times can contribute to obtaining different minimal subsets.
claim.scope: Possible variability in reduction results, not an observed effect in these cases.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly identifies variable return times as a possible contributor to different minimal subsets.

signal_basis.value: A reduced configuration repeatedly reproduces lateness, while specified further removals cease to reproduce it. Reduction decisions depend on these outcomes under controlled test conditions, with inconsistent outcomes classified as unresolved.
signal_basis.scope: The selected replay and its tested configurations; this signal does not establish that return-time variation actually changed any resulting subset.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the reproduction pattern, outcome-dependent retention rule, controlled comparisons and treatment of inconsistent outcomes; P004 defines lateness.
The claim is supported as a bounded possibility and requires no conditional empirical relation.

rationale: Return timing can affect whether a configuration misses the start deadline, and reduction retains configurations according to that outcome. Different return timings can therefore change which combinations preserve failure and which minimal subsets result. Holding conditions fixed within a comparison does not establish invariance across return-time conditions. This licenses the stated possibility without demonstrating an actual effect.
uncertainty: The signal does not determine whether return-time variation affected these cases or how large such an effect would be.
